full_judgment:
K.M. Subhan, J.-This Rule is directed against the order passed on 25-3-75 by the learned District Judge, Dinajpur in Miscellaneous case No. 42 of 1973 which arose gut of Title Appeal No, 47 of 1966. 

 The opposite party instituted a title suit against the petitioners for declaration of title and recovery of possession of the suit lands. A written statement was filed on behalf of the defendant Nos. 2 to 4, 6 to 8 and 16 and another set of written statement was filed on behalf of the defendants Nos. 5 and 9 to 15 while defendant No. 1 (ka) filed yet another written statement to contest the suit. The learned Subordinate Judge framed 4 Issues for the trial of the suit, but no issue was framed on the question of limitation though this question was specifically pleaded by all the defendants. The learned Subordinate Judge by his judgment and decree dated 30-6-66 decreed the suit from which an appeal was preferred before the learned District Judge being Title Appeal No. 47 of 1966 and the learned District Judge by his judgment and order allowed the appeal and remanded the suit to the learned Subordinate Judge for deciding the question of limitation on the pleadings and evidence on record. The question that was sent down for consideration of the learned Subordinate Judge was framed as "whether the suit is barred by limitation". From the said order of remand by the learned District Judge, the present petitioners and the deceased defendants preferred a Second Miscellaneous Appeal being No. 12 of 1968 which was finally disposed of by a Division Bench of this Court on 9-4-73. The High Court Division allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and order of the learned District Judge who was directed to follow the procedure as laid down in order 41, rule 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure, keeping the appeal pending in his Court. During the pendency of the aforesaid Second Miscellaneous Appeal before this Court 4 of the 16 appellants died, but their legal heirs were not brought on record by substitution or otherwise, which was purely due to the ignorance of the other appellants as to the requirements of law as provided for in the Code. 

 In this particular case since the heirs were not substituted due to the ignorance of the appellants of the deaths of the defendant’s appeals as against them abated. The provisions of the Code does not due to the ignorance of the appellants exempt abatement caused by deaths and keep the appeal alive Mr. M.H. Khandkar, the learned Advocate has referred to the decision of Mohammad Wajid Ali Khan Vs. Puran Singh& others, reported in A.I.R. 1929 P.C. 58and also the decision of Misri Lal Nair Vs. Most. Suraj reported in A.I.R. 1958 P.C. 28 These two decisions, however are on different points and have no application to the facts of this case.
